requirements.text: escalate their existing case for this product
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 700 AND account_id = 31 AND product_id = 83 AND escalation = 1 AND escalation_reason = 'customer_request' AND priority = 'moderate'
requirements.source: Verify if the case escalated correctly.
assumptions: Cooper PLC is account 31 and Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 Variant 63 is product 83; case 700 is the account's only case for that product, so no choice by priority arises
escalation_reason customer_request: the client itself called asking for the urgent fix, and the policy requires customer_request when the customer escalates, ahead of vip or urgency
priority moderate (unchanged from the seed) kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy

requirements.text: assign it to Daniel Hanson (email - daniel.hanson@servicenow.com) as he is free and belongs to the same group(Returns Authorization Desk_3)
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 700 AND account_id = 31 AND product_id = 83 AND assignment_group_id = 55 AND assigned_to = 103 AND priority = 'moderate'
requirements.source: Verify case is assigned to the correct user as requested.
assumptions: Daniel Hanson is user 103 by the email given, an active agent and a member of Returns Authorization Desk_3, so the policy's assignment constraints hold
Returns Authorization Desk_3 is group 55, the case's group on the seed; the request keeps the case in that group, since Daniel Hanson is chosen for belonging to it
priority moderate (unchanged from the seed) kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy

requirements.text: escalate their existing case for this product
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE account_id = 31 AND case_id <> 700 AND escalation = 1
assumptions: only the case for this product is escalated; a loose reading of 'their existing case' for a VIP client would sweep in the account's other cases, including case 706 for the near-named product Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9
one other Cooper PLC case (708, closed) is escalated on the seed, so the count stays at 1

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 706 AND assigned_to IS NULL
assumptions: case 706 is Cooper PLC's case for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 (product 3), a name that nearly matches the product asked about; it is not reassigned

notes:
Merged from two passes that agree on case 700 (account 31, product 83), escalation_reason customer_request, Daniel Hanson (user 103) in group 55, priority moderate, and both dispositions (kept).
disagreement: boundary stay on the other Cooper PLC cases: one pass keeps the escalation count of all the account's other cases at its seed value, the other anchors case 706 (the near-named product Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9) and tests that it stays unescalated and unassigned; kept both parts as two stays, the wider escalation stay because it is the tighter test and a loose reading of 'their existing case' for a VIP client would escalate the account's other cases, and the assignment test on case 706 because 'assign it' could sweep in the near-named product's case; the escalation of case 706 is carried by the wider stay.
The request gives the client's VIP status as the motive for escalating, which could suggest escalation_reason vip; the client's own call asking for an urgent fix makes this a customer escalation, and the policy fixes customer_request for that case, which the benchmark also tests.
The policy asks for the escalation's justification to be logged in case notes, but the database has no case-notes table or column and no listed tool writes notes, so that step is untestable.
The request does not ask for the client's call to be recorded as an interaction, and no listed tool writes that table.
Nicole Pineda (user 503) is the previous assignee on the seed; the request only replaces her on case 700, so her own records are not tested.
